_comment: The vendor modules this machine has. Hand-maintained - it is the main repo's
single statement of which control platforms exist and which version of each was
verified against this twin. A module is a SEPARATE repository the user clones
into this repo's root; the path is gitignored so the two git repos do not collide.
Three tools read this file: build_knowledge.py (which vendor links to emit),
build_wiki.py (which sibling wikis to link into, and where) and
check_compatibility.py (the pairing table). Adding a vendor is one entry here plus
a repository - no tool changes.
`tested` is the module version this twin was actually verified against. ONE field,
and a fact rather than a promise: it is the version to clone. There is deliberately
no version RANGE here and no `requiresMain` in a module - a range admits versions
that do not exist yet, so nobody ever narrows one and it never catches anything.
Whether a module is actually current is answered exactly, and without anyone
maintaining it, by comparing the machine handoff it committed against this repo's
_docs/context/.machine.json. See COMPATIBILITY.md.
`knowledgeBase` says whether the module publishes _docs/ pages that a root page
can link to - and therefore whether it has a wiki of its own to link into. It is
DECLARED rather than probed for, because these pages are tracked: deriving it from
what is on disk would make a tracked file's content depend on which optional
modules a given user happened to clone.
